Flash has been made obsolete by HTML5, apparently. As far as I know, there is no Flash for mobile. If you need Flash on desktop, just install it.

Flash has been almost entirely replaced; websites now should be using HTML5 and CSS for displaying content and JS for making it interactive or otherwise animated programmatically.

The one major omission, absolutely insane given today's media market, is live video (I would guess that is your application / reason for asking). There are JS-backed players which can show live video given some server code/setup to provide a dynamic playlist of chunked video files, though this is really just a clever workaround which won't surpass Flash live video as a stable, low-delay solution until HTML5 gets its shit together. I think the basic problem is that browsers work by retrieving files via HTTP GET whereas live video really needs UDP broadcasts or at least just a raw TCP connection, both of which are locked down by browsers but not by applets in a browser.
